summary:
OUR SIDE. The pipeline entry point is test_full_pipeline.py; its loop is time bounded, not replan bounded (no replan cap since audit #107). 'Planning time' is the perf_counter span around planner.plan() per replan (test_full_pipeline.py:1322-1352), with a disposal replan folded into the same plan_dt when a mission plan fails while holding (1379-1400); plan() builds the PDDLStream problem and calls solve(algorithm='adaptive', max_time, search_sample_ratio) (pddlstream_planner.py:1004-1010, 1131-1150), so the number includes stream sampling, FastDownward searches and PDDLStream's busy wait, all wall clock. Execution time is NOT recorded as its own field anywhere; timing_summary.json (run_logger.py:432-464) carries run_config, success, exit_reason, plan_count, n_sense_actions, total_planning_time_s, per_call_planning_time_s, physical failure lists, integrity events, giveup sets, boxel counts and init fact counts, and the runner adds wall_clock_s = perf_counter around the whole subprocess (interpreter start, scene build, pre-flight probe, execution, teardown; eval_runner.py:578-600, 656). Execution can only be inferred as wall minus planning minus overhead. Budgets: --max-plan-time default 1800 s per plan() call (run_logger.py:714-722); eval_runner --timeout default 300 s per cell, CB#113 ran at 1800 (eval_runner.py:813-815; PAPER_AUDIT.txt:744); tools/_eval_ab.py --timeout 1200 s per episode. The '900 s cap' in the task text is a historical cap hit in specific runs (run_logger.py:638, pddlstream_planner.py:989, 1145), not a current default. Success for holding = belief.is_target_found() AND the simulator check _verify_holding; stack goals = goal_satisfied AND _verify_goal_physics AABB checks (test_full_pipeline.py:2275-2307). Exit reasons: all_searched, pick_giveup, no_plan_while_holding, planner_failed, no_plan_binding_death, drop_failed, knocked_off_table, target_lost, stack_giveup, physics_mismatch, timeout (default when the loop ended without a reason), plus runner stubs timeout, crash_exitN, preflight_rejected, no_summary, summary_mismatch (run_logger.py:285-383; eval_runner.py:588-650). Exit code 0 success, 1 failure, 2 env misconfiguration; pre-flight rejections exit 1 with a '[pre-flight] seed N rejected' stderr line and no run directory; there is no seed re-roll of any kind since 2026-08-23. The runner is a subprocess per cell with --no-telemetry because telemetry costs wall clock. The CB#113 pattern: the sweep runs from an immutable snapshot directory (<git>\Semantic_Boxels_sweep_cb113, no .git, 47 entries) while results land in the main repo at eval_results/sweep_cb113 with the commit in eval_results/sweep_cb113.commit (430a214), resumable with --skip-existing; 491 of 2160 cells are banked, the last cell was written 2026-09-22, so it is paused, not running, but any new run must still pgrep first. Hazards recorded: one pipeline process at a time (pddlstream temp/ race), host sleep stalls cells (monotonic vs wall clocks disagree; tools/_sweep_drop_stalled_cells.py cleans them), a result-banking bug fixed 2026-10-24 that credited pre-flight-rejected cells with the previous cell's success. Measured noise floor: identical code flips 1 to 2 seeds per 20 (f2021c vs f2021b, PAPER_AUDIT.txt:2512-2522); six same-quality configs spread 11 to 17 of 20 (eval SKILL.md:121-125); time comparisons need back-to-back arms on an idle machine.

THEIR SIDE. run_planner.py seeds random and numpy with --global-seed, builds the env, calls env.initialize(), then policy.rollout (run_planner.py:125-138). initialize() picks the scene with random.choice(os.listdir('tampura_environments/find_dice/problems')) (env.py:802-803); the directory holds exactly 3 JSON scenes, so the 20 seeds are 20 stochastic trials over 3 layouts, and the seed-to-scene map depends on the filesystem listing order (recorded per run by the 'Loading scene from X.json' console line). Scene A (1747173590.312597.json, die + 4 cups) got seeds 1,2,3,4,8,14,15,18 and 2/8 successes; scene B (1747173591.670785.json, die + 1 cup) got seeds 0,7,9,11,12,13,16 and 6/7; scene C (1747173593.826745.json, die + 4 cups) got seeds 5,6,10,17,19 and 3/5. The rollout runs exactly max_steps=20 steps, never terminates early, and takes no-op once the reward is 1 (policy.py:105-153; tampura_policy.py:77-80). time_deltas is a cumulative time.time() clock from loop start; loop_s = time_deltas[-1] covers get_action (flat stream sampling, 200 outcome samples in batches of 20, SymK, LAO*) plus env.step execution plus belief update, and excludes process start, env.initialize and the pickle save (policy.py:104,136,153; tampura_sweep.py:191). wall_s is the sweep driver's perf_counter around the subprocess (tampura_sweep.py:151-161). symk_solve_s is a regex sum of SymK 'Time:' lines, 0.04 to 1.5 s per episode, so SymK is negligible and outcome sampling dominates (tqdm: 58 s at t=0 seed 0, 96 s at t=0 seed 1). success = rewards[-1] == 1.0 where reward = Exists(is-target AND holding) AND at-home evaluated on the abstract BELIEF (env.py:993-1004; spec.py:140-143); holding comes from belief.grasp, which pick_execute_fn sets after IK and a motion plan succeed, with no physical grasp check (env.py:368-397), and at-home from current_conf within 1e-4 of DEFAULT_ARM_POS (env.py:318-321). In headless mode their trajectories are teleported, not stepped (panda_env_utils.py:928), which makes headless loop_s partly kinematic. Per-episode timeout 900 s is the driver's subprocess kill, never hit in the 05-26 run (max 742.58 s); TAMPURA has no internal time budget. find_dice.yml: max_steps 20, batch_size 20, num_skeletons 10, flat_sample true, flat_width 5, pwa 0.2, pwk 3.0, envelope_threshold 1, num_samples 200, gamma 0.98, bayes_optimistic, decision prob, symk unordered/fw/simple, from_scratch true (default.yml differs: max_steps 10, batch 10, flat_sample false, num_samples 100, gamma 0.95). Failures typically loop the same infeasible look action under envelope continuation to step 20 (seed_1.log, seed_18.log). Aggregate 2026-05-26: 11/20 = 55 %, loop_s all 239.9 +/- 151.1 s, success-only 166.1 +/- 84.7 s (n=11), wall_s all 253.3 +/- 150.9 s. The published 57 +/- 38 s is a PER-STEP time including simulated controller execution on the authors' Xeon Gold 6248 and must not be compared against per-episode numbers; the thesis already states this (results.tex:295, 399-402; eval_plotter.py:1112-1139 hardcodes TAMPURA_MEAN 166 / STD 85 / N 11 from the local run).

PROTOCOL. Both arms in one campaign, serial, interleaved per seed, idle machine, keep awake, pgrep first; TAMPURA's seeds 0-19 unchanged with the scene file logged per seed on both arms and results stratified by scene; success for BOTH systems = their get_reward on their abstract belief produced through their execute_fn observation channel; identical per-episode wall cap (900 s as in tampura_sweep.py) stated in the paper, our --max-plan-time at or below it; report success with Wilson 95 % intervals, per-episode loop time (all and success-only), process wall, and per-action time = loop time / non-no-op actions executed; our planning-only time reported as an extra that TAMPURA cannot produce without harness-side instrumentation; at least two repetitions of the 20-seed block per arm; the 05-26 run is a reproduction check of the TAMPURA arm, not the comparison row. Outputs go to eval_results/tampura_bridge_<date>/ in the repo (TAMPURA run dirs live on the WSL side under /root/tampura-work/tampura_environments/runs and must be copied over; never /tmp), with a campaign.json recording both commits (ours; tampura cdddf14b; tampura_environments 4167c35e), the find_dice.yml snapshot, caps, CPU and PYTHONHASHSEED. Every headless command is paired with its GUI twin (tampura_run_gui.sh SEED 1; ours with --vis 1 as an int flag, because their --vis uses type=bool and '--vis=0' still opens the GUI).

facts.claim: Our per-replan planning time is the perf_counter span around planner.plan(), accumulated into total_plan_time and plan_times; a disposal replan after a no-plan-while-holding is folded into the same plan_dt.

planner.plan() builds the PDDLStream problem and calls solve(algorithm='adaptive', max_time=..., unit_costs, planner, search_sample_ratio), so 'planning time' is PDDLStream wall clock including stream sampling, FastDownward and the adaptive loop's busy wait.

timing_summary.json keys: run_config, success, exit_reason, plan_count, n_sense_actions, total_planning_time_s, per_call_planning_time_s, physical_failures_per_action, physical_failures_at_goal, integrity_events, n_integrity_events, integrity_event_kinds, stack_fail_counts, blocked_giveup_shadows, pick_giveup_objects, boxel_counts_per_replan, n_object_boxels, n_shadow_boxels, n_free_space_boxels, boxel_volumes_object/shadow/free_space, n_init_state_facts, n_facts_by_predicate. No execution-time field exists.
The console prints 'Cumulative planning time : X.XXXs' and 'Plans executed: N', which tools/_eval_ab.py parses by regex; _eval_ab success requires 'SUCCESS' in output AND exit code 0 AND no timeout.

eval_runner wall_clock_s is perf_counter around the whole subprocess (interpreter start to exit) and is written into the copied summary; cells run one at a time in a loop; --timeout default 300 s per cell; a timed-out cell is a stub row with exit_reason 'timeout'.
eval_runner passes --no-telemetry to every cell because the world telemetry recorder samples the simulator every step and would shift the wall clock the sweep measures.
--max-plan-time default is 1800 s per PDDLStream call; the 900 s figures in the code are historical cap hits (ff-astar1 seed 999; tray smoke plan 6), not a current default.
The main loop has no replan cap; it ends on goal, a give-up, planner no-plan, or the runner's per-cell wall-clock kill.

Holding success = belief.is_target_found() AND _verify_holding(env, target, held_body_id); stack/tray success = goal_satisfied AND _verify_goal_physics; a failed physics check reclassifies exit_reason to physics_mismatch.

Exit reasons printed by report_run_outcome: all_searched, pick_giveup, no_plan_while_holding, planner_failed, no_plan_binding_death, drop_failed, knocked_off_table, target_lost, stack_giveup, physics_mismatch; None becomes 'timeout'. Runner stubs add crash_exitN, preflight_rejected, no_summary, summary_mismatch.

test_full_pipeline exits 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 when numpy is missing; a pre-flight rejection prints '[pre-flight] seed N rejected: ...' to stderr and re-raises (exit 1, no run directory); seed re-roll was removed 2026-08-23.
Our --seed seeds random and numpy once (random.seed(args.seed); np.random.seed(args.seed)) and is passed to the scene builders.

run_config written into the summary includes scene, n_occluders, n_targets, n_hidden, seed, goal, planner, sense_gate, baseline, min_boxel_size, gui, log_level and more; the runner refuses a summary whose run_config does not match the cell (summary_mismatch).
A result-banking bug (a pre-flight-rejected cell banked the previous cell's summary when it finished within 1 s) was found and fixed 2026-10-24; CB#113 had 10 phantom holding successes from it.

CB#113 launched 2026-09-20 on commit 430a214 from an immutable snapshot directory Semantic_Boxels_sweep_cb113 with --timeout 1800 --skip-existing, output eval_results/sweep_cb113 in the main repo, commit recorded in eval_results/sweep_cb113.commit; concurrent pipeline runs contend for CPU and shift pddlstream's wall-clock budgets.

The snapshot directory <git>\Semantic_Boxels_sweep_cb113 exists with 47 top-level entries and no .git (consistent with an archive export); the exact command used to create it is not written in PAPER_AUDIT.
facts.evidence: PowerShell listing 2026-10-25; PAPER_AUDIT.txt:742-746 (grep for 'git archive' found nothing)

facts.claim: CB#113 has 491 cells banked of 2160 (aggregated.csv 492 lines incl. header, re-aggregated 2026-10-24); the newest cell directory is dated 2026-09-22, so the sweep is paused, not running.

Host sleep stalls a sweep: the runner's per-cell timeout is a monotonic deadline that does not advance during suspend, while pddlstream's 'Time:' counter is wall clock; stalled cells bank 'timeout' rows that are not data; tools/_sweep_drop_stalled_cells.py removes cells whose wall clock exceeds 1.5x the 1800 s timeout.
One pipeline process at a time: the /eval skill requires 'pgrep -af test_full_pipeline' before any run because of the pddlstream temp/ race; concurrent GUI runs caused abrupt deaths.

Measured noise floor for identical planning code: f2021c_51fd444 14/20 vs f2021b_ba924bd 15/20 with three seed flips (0 won; 1 and 8 lost), attributed to ~0.2 s of extra wall clock moving PDDLStream's wall-clock budgets; recorded as +/-1-2 seeds per 20 for the SAME code.

The /eval skill states that at n=20 a difference of +/-2-3 seeds is noise (six same-quality configs spread 11-17/20 on 2026-08-22) and that time comparisons need arms run back-to-back on an otherwise idle machine.

CB#112 (Wilson intervals) is PARKED and no Wilson implementation exists in the repo's Python files; CB#111 (TAMPURA wall-clock plot regen) and CB#125 (stale eval_plotter docstring) are assigned to #P4 after PHASE 4.
facts.evidence: PAPER_AUDIT.txt:3307-3309, 3318, 3196-3199; grep -i wilson over *.py returned no matches

facts.claim: eval_plotter.plot_tampura_wallclock_comparison hardcodes TAMPURA_MEAN=166.0, TAMPURA_STD=85.0, TAMPURA_N=11 (success-only loop time from runs/sweep_2026-05-26.json) and deliberately does not plot the published 57 +/- 38 s because that is per-step including simulated controller execution.

The thesis frames the comparison as per-episode on the same hardware (144.4 s ours vs 166 s TAMPURA, success-only), notes the published 57 s is per-step, says the Find Die dataset ships three fixed scene layouts drawn at random per episode, and names the hardware (Ryzen 7 PRO 7730U vs authors' Xeon Gold 6248).

TAMPURA per-seed baseline (sweep_2026-05-26.json): success 11/20 = 0.55; wall_s all mean 253.349 std 150.927 min 95.821 max 742.58; loop_s all mean 239.901 std 151.094; wall_s success-only mean 179.518 std 84.117 (n=11); loop_s success-only mean 166.053 std 84.652; symk_solve_s all mean 0.457.

metric_notes: wall_s = full subprocess wall clock (perf_counter, includes Python+pybullet startup/teardown); loop_s = RolloutHistory.time_deltas[-1] (planning + pybullet action execution inside the policy loop, excludes process startup/teardown); symk_solve_s = best-effort sum of SymK 'Time:' values; success iff rewards[-1] == 1.0; solve_step = first index where reward becomes 1.0.

time_deltas is a cumulative time.time() clock started just before the step loop; each step appends time.time() - st after get_action, env.step and belief update; the final entry is appended after the last step. env.initialize() and save_run_data are outside it.

The rollout always runs exactly max_steps iterations (no early termination); once the abstract belief has reward > 0 the policy returns no-op without planning; n_actions in the sweep JSON counts no-ops (only the trailing None is excluded), hence 20 for every seed.

TAMPURA reward = And([Exists(is-target(?o) AND holding(?o)), at-home]) evaluated on the abstract belief; holding comes from belief.grasp/grasp_body, at-home from current_conf within rtol/atol 1e-4 of DEFAULT_ARM_POS.

pick_execute_fn sets obs.grasp/grasp_body only after grasp_ik and plan_motion succeed and pick_execute ran; there is no physical check that the die is in the gripper (pick_execute closes to grasp.closed_position and sets state.grasp). home_execute_fn returns conf=DEFAULT_ARM_POS in the observation even when plan_motion fails (motion_plan None returns the same observation).

In headless mode TAMPURA teleports along trajectories instead of stepping them (teleport = not pbu.has_gui(...)), so headless loop_s under-counts physical execution relative to a GUI run (seed 0: ~70 s headless vs ~110 s GUI).

Their perception: obs_from_camera_image reads the segmentation mask body ids from the rendered camera image and, for each visible body, takes its pose from world.poses (ground truth pose of visible objects only).

The seed controls everything: run_planner seeds random and numpy with global_seed before env construction; initialize() draws the scene with random.choice(os.listdir('tampura_environments/find_dice/problems')); the directory holds exactly 3 JSON scenes; the remaining RNG draws drive flat stream sampling, outcome sampling and motion planning.

Seed-to-scene map of the 05-26 run from the 'Loading scene from' console line: 1747173590.312597.json (die + b,e,d,a cups) seeds 1,2,3,4,8,14,15,18; 1747173591.670785.json (d_cups_ud + die) seeds 0,7,9,11,12,13,16; 1747173593.826745.json (a,d,e cups, die, b cup) seeds 5,6,10,17,19.
facts.evidence: wsl_tampura\sweep_consoles\seed_N.log:4 for all 20 seeds; categories at seed_1.log:9, seed_0.log:9, seed_5.log:9

facts.claim: Per-scene TAMPURA success: scene 1747173590 2/8 (seeds 2, 4), scene 1747173591 6/7 (seed 16 failed), scene 1747173593 3/5 (seeds 5, 10 failed).
facts.evidence: sweep_2026-05-26.json per_seed success fields joined with the seed-to-scene map above

facts.claim: find_dice.yml used by the sweep: max_steps 20, batch_size 20, num_skeletons 10, flat_sample true, flat_width 5, pwa 0.2, pwk 3.0, envelope_threshold 1, num_samples 200, gamma 0.98, planner tampura_policy, learning bayes_optimistic, decision prob, symk unordered/fw/simple, from_scratch true; the snapshot is embedded in the sweep JSON. default.yml differs (max_steps 10, batch 10, flat_sample false, flat_width 1, num_samples 100, gamma 0.95).

With envelope_threshold 1 and from_scratch true the policy resets F/R and re-samples 200 outcomes whenever the envelope probability is below 1; when the envelope holds it only re-solves the MDP, which is why seed 1 repeated look(o_ph_0, o_ph_4, o_co_14) from t=5 to t=19 with no Outcome Sampling line.
Outcome sampling dominates TAMPURA's time (tqdm 58 s at t=0 for seed 0, 96 s at t=0 for seed 1) while SymK solve lines are 0.01 to 0.04 s each; symk_solve_s is therefore not a planning-time measure.

tampura_sweep.py runs one isolated subprocess per seed with --per-episode-timeout 900, prepends the venv bin to PATH (SymK shells out to bare python), writes an atomic resumable JSON after every seed, and parses success from the newest RolloutHistory pickle in the new run directory. No seed timed out in the 05-26 run.
facts.evidence: wsl_tampura\tampura_sweep.py:111, 125-130, 143-215; sweep_2026-05-26.json timed_out fields all false

facts.claim: TAMPURA has no internal time budget: neither tampura_policy.py nor solvers/symk.py reference time or timeout; the episode budget is max_steps and the external subprocess kill.
facts.evidence: grep over <git>\tampura\tampura\policies\tampura_policy.py and solvers\symk.py for time./timeout/max_time returned no matches

facts.claim: The 05-26 sweep was run on a Ryzen 7 PRO 7730U (8 cores) in WSL2 Ubuntu, single uninterrupted session; an earlier 05-25 sweep was discarded because a Windows suspend inflated one seed's time_deltas to ~9 h.

The published 57 +/- 38 s is per-step including simulated controller execution (Table II caption, arXiv 2403.10454 v2 p.15), averaged over trials and steps; the published success >= 0.63 is inferred from the discounted return.

GUI run command for TAMPURA: bash /root/tampura-work/tampura_run_gui.sh SEED VIS_GRAPH runs run_planner.py --config=./env_configs/find_dice.yml --vis=1 --global-seed=SEED --vis-graph=...; headless must OMIT --vis because argparse type=bool makes '--vis=0' truthy.

The archived bridge wrote success into their belief directly: belief_bridge.mark_holding sets belief.grasp/grasp_body and mark_at_home sets current_conf = DEFAULT_ARM_POS; boxel_policy.go_home discarded execute_go_home's status and set info['success'] = True unconditionally (CB#123).

The archived bridge's launch pattern injected our repo and pddlstream_lib via PYTHONPATH into their venv with cwd = their env repo: '... cd /root/tampura-work/tampura_environments && PYTHONPATH=/mnt/c/.../Semantic_Boxels:/mnt/c/.../pddlstream_lib python /mnt/c/.../tampura_bridge/run_boxel_on_finddice.py --global-seed 0 --vis 1', seeding random/numpy with global_seed and calling env.initialize() exactly as run_planner.py does.
The Windows TAMPURA mirrors are at tampura main = cdddf14b45d2608fc1d3bc9c72d8ee249c4638b2 and tampura_environments main = 4167c35e41170beee48b108d4a6a64a69d4b555a.

eval_corpus.json is our pre-vetted seed list (schema_version 1, audit 77, n_corpus 192 after the 2026-09-20 re-probe) over random-pairs probe configs; it is irrelevant to TAMPURA's seeds, which are fixed at 0-19 by their convention.

The thesis's holding goal does not require go-home while find_dice's reward does; the archived plan flagged this one-action asymmetry and the archived bridge added at_home/go_home to its domain variant.

The _eval_ab per-arm JSON is {arm, branch, head, scene, goal, pipeline_args, results[]} with per-episode fields seed, effective_seed, rerolls, success, timed_out, exit_code, plans_executed, planning_time_s, senses_seen, wall_s, fail_reason, integrity_events, bystander_events, transit_losses, direct_path_certified, direct_path_rejected; results are persisted after every episode and resumed by seed.

design_relevant_details: TAMPURA AGGREGATES: success 11/20 = 0.55; wall_s all 253.349 +/- 150.927 (min 95.821, max 742.58); loop_s all 239.901 +/- 151.094 (min 81.794, max 728.948); wall_s success-only 179.518 +/- 84.117 (n=11); loop_s success-only 166.053 +/- 84.652 (n=11); symk_solve_s all 0.457 +/- 0.544. Per scene: 1747173590 (die + 4 cups) 2/8; 1747173591 (die + 1 cup) 6/7; 1747173593 (die + 4 cups) 3/5. Only 3 scene layouts exist; report results stratified by scene and say so in the paper (thesis already does, results.tex:394-397).

TAMPURA METRIC DEFINITIONS: loop_s = RolloutHistory.time_deltas[-1], a cumulative time.time() clock over the 20-step loop covering get_action (planning: flat stream sampling, 200 outcome samples in batches of 20 policy_search calls, SymK, LAO*) + env.step (execution) + belief update; it excludes env.initialize (scene build, first render) and the pickle save. wall_s = subprocess perf_counter including interpreter start and teardown. Per-step deltas are obtainable by differencing time_deltas; post-goal no-op steps cost ~0. symk_solve_s (sum of 'Time:' lines, 0.04-1.5 s) is SymK only and must never be presented as TAMPURA planning time. 'Planning-only' time for TAMPURA is not separable from the pickle (TAMPURA_PLAN_HEAD.md:229-231); it needs a harness-side wrapper around policy.get_action and env.step (subclass or decorator in OUR code, their files untouched) if the paper wants that column.

TAMPURA SUCCESS CRITERION (use it verbatim for BOTH systems): rewards[-1] == 1.0 where reward = problem_spec.get_reward(b.abstract(store), store), reward expression And([Exists(is-target(?o) AND holding(?o)), at-home]) (env.py:993-1004). holding is belief.grasp set by their pick_execute_fn after IK + motion plan + executed close (no physical grasp verification, env.py:368-397); at-home is current_conf within 1e-4 of DEFAULT_ARM_POS, set by their home_execute_fn observation (env.py:563-581). For our system the terminal belief must be produced through THEIR execute_fn observation channel (env.step -> b.update), never by writing belief.grasp / current_conf from our side (the CB#123 anti-pattern, archive/tampura_bridge_v1/belief_bridge.py:44-58). Optionally add OUR _verify_holding-style simulator check as a stricter secondary column, reported separately, never replacing theirs.

TAMPURA BUDGETS: max_steps 20 (episode always runs 20 steps, no early stop), num_samples 200 / batch_size 20 per re-sample, envelope_threshold 1 + from_scratch true (re-sample from scratch whenever the envelope probability < 1), no internal time limit; external per-episode kill 900 s in tampura_sweep.py (never hit in 05-26, max 742.58 s). State both the 20-step cap and the 900 s cap in the paper.

OUR BUDGETS TO MATCH: eval_runner --timeout (per-cell wall, default 300 s; CB#113 1800 s), _eval_ab --timeout 1200 s, --max-plan-time 1800 s per PDDLStream call (run_logger.py:714-722), no replan cap. For the bridge campaign choose ONE per-episode wall cap for both arms (900 s mirrors tampura_sweep.py; 1800 s mirrors CB#113) and set our --max-plan-time at or below it so a single plan() cannot outlive the episode. Our loop is time bounded while theirs is step bounded; record our executed action count per episode so a per-action time exists, and decide (and record in the audit) whether to also impose a 20-action cap on ours.

OUR METRIC DEFINITIONS: total_planning_time_s = sum of perf_counter spans around planner.plan() (PDDLStream solve incl. streams + FD + problem build), per_call_planning_time_s list, plan_count, n_sense_actions; wall_clock_s = runner perf_counter around the subprocess; execution time is not recorded (derive wall - planning - startup, or add an explicit loop clock in the bridge harness mirroring time_deltas: start just before the first plan(), stamp after every executed action, so an apples-to-apples 'loop time' exists on both sides). Console markers parsed by _eval_ab: 'SUCCESS', 'Plans executed: N', 'Cumulative planning time : Xs', 'FAILED: ...'.

OUR RESULT SCHEMA: timing_summary.json per run (run_logger.py:432-464) copied into <sweep>/cells/<tag>/timing_summary.json with wall_clock_s added and run_dir.txt + stdout.log beside it; <sweep>/matrix.json; aggregated.csv (PRIMARY_COLUMNS scene, n_occluders, n_targets, n_hidden, seed, goal, unit_costs, baseline, uniform_cell_size, success, exit_reason, plan_count, total_planning_time_s, wall_clock_s + sorted extras) and aggregated.jsonl (list-valued fields kept). _eval_ab per-arm JSON {arm, branch, head, scene, goal, pipeline_args, results[...]} in eval_results/ab_eval/<tag>.json. A bridge campaign should emit one JSON per arm with the same per-seed shape as sweep_2026-05-26.json (seed, success, wall_s, loop_s, solve_step, n_actions, rewards, returncode, timed_out, run_dir, console_log, note, _complete, plus scene_file and, for ours, planning_time_s, plan_count, exit_reason) so one report script reads both.

RESULT INTEGRITY RULES already learned the hard way: bind every banked result to its seed (only a run directory created during the cell; run_config/seed must match; a pre-flight-style rejection is its own exit_reason), never 'newest file within 1 s' (eval_runner.py:475-499, PAPER_AUDIT.txt:772-793). Both TAMPURA's driver and ours identify the run dir by set difference of directories before/after launch (tampura_sweep.py:148, 168-170; eval_runner.py:579, 619).

honesty_risks: Belief writes as success: the archived bridge set belief.grasp / grasp_body / current_conf directly (belief_bridge.mark_holding, mark_at_home) and marked info['success'] = True regardless of execute_go_home's status (CB#123). Any path where our code writes into their SceneBelief fields that feed get_reward is an oracle write; success must come only from observations their execute_fn returns through env.step.

Teleporting the die or arm (resetBasePositionAndOrientation of task objects, or setting joint states to DEFAULT_ARM_POS without a motion plan) to make at-home or holding true; their home_execute_fn already reports conf=DEFAULT_ARM_POS even when plan_motion fails (env.py:566-579), so a bridge that mirrors that leniency without actually moving the arm would inflate at-home. Report go_home no_path as a failure.

Reading poses of hidden objects: their obs_from_camera_image hands out ground truth poses only for bodies present in the segmentation mask (env.py:64-75). Reading world.poses (or PyBullet poses) for the die before it is visible, or matching body ids to find 'the die', is an oracle read; the planner must discover the die by relocating cups and sensing.

Scene or seed specific code: fixed names like 'cup_0', hardcoded die pose, ordering assumptions about which of the 3 problem JSONs a seed loads, or per-seed parameter changes. Only 3 layouts exist, so a solution tuned on one layout masquerades as general; stratify by scene and keep the code scene-generic.

Retry-until-success or seed re-rolls: the archived _replan retried the solve up to 5 times; any retry must be bounded identically for all seeds, counted inside loop time, and disclosed; re-rolling a seed, re-running a failed seed, or excluding seeds is cherry picking (seed re-roll was removed from the main pipeline 2026-08-23 for this reason).

Plan post-processing or scripted decisions: nothing may edit the action sequence between solve() and the executor; park-before-sense, cup-choice heuristics, or 'look under the nearest cup' scripts are the previous bridge's failure mode (H2). WHAT/WHERE/ORDER decisions must be literal planner outputs computed from the belief.

Asymmetric budgets or settings: giving ours a larger per-episode cap than TAMPURA's, changing find_dice.yml (num_samples, batch_size, max_steps) for the TAMPURA arm, running TAMPURA under contention while ours runs idle, or running the two arms weeks apart on different machine states. The 05-26 run is a reproduction check, not the comparison row.

Metric mismatch: comparing our per-episode numbers to the published per-step 57 s; comparing our planning-only time to TAMPURA's symk_solve_s (SymK is ~0.5 s of a ~240 s episode); reporting success-only times without all-episode times; counting TAMPURA's post-goal no-ops as actions or our idle time differently; mixing headless teleported execution (theirs) with stepped physics (ours) without disclosure.

Harness banking errors: 'newest file within 1 s' summary matching credited rejected cells with the previous cell's success in CB#113; any new harness must bind results to seed via run_config and directory set difference, and treat a missing result as a failure row, never as a skip.

Host sleep and clock mix: time.time() (TAMPURA time_deltas, pddlstream budgets) advances across suspend while monotonic deadlines do not; a slept episode produces hours-long loop_s or an unkilled run; drop and re-run such episodes with the rule written down beforehand (1.5x cap), never post hoc selection.
Naming and prose: never call the adaptation 'faithful'; use neutral verbs (execute_pick, execute_go_home); no dashes in user-facing prose.

Silent model tweaks: a containment/'look underneath' region type, a go-home action, or a relaxed pick precondition each change the system under test; each needs its own audit entry with before/after and the thesis claim it touches (H3) before any number is quoted.
